complex_logic: The generation pipeline manages a multi-step tool loop with a token-capacity retry ladder, write-epoch guards at every file-write callsite, parallel post-generation validation passes, repair-pass budget tracking, and streaming to clients, all resumable across a serverless hibernation and wake cycle.

A transactional quota ledger holds concurrent-generation leases and daily call and output-token counters inside a single atomic database write, eliminating the time-of-check and time-of-use gap between the concurrency cap check, the daily cap check, and the actual lease insertion.

Monotonic write-epoch tickets require that each file-write callsite hold the current generation's ticket; any write arriving with an older ticket is silently discarded, preventing stale file contents from landing after a user stops one generation and immediately starts another.

An outbound-request guard checks every custom provider address and every agent fetch-tool target against a strict ruleset that rejects non-encrypted schemes, all private and link-local network address literals, and re-validates the resolved destination after any redirect before allowing the request.

The user account registry manages project ownership, per-user project and storage quotas, publication state with name-uniqueness and hosted-slot accounting, per-model admin kill-switches, and gallery remix cap enforcement, all within atomic database transactions to preserve invariants under concurrent requests.
substantial_features: A full authentication overhaul carried across many commits replaced a zero-auth design with cryptographically signed session tokens, secure credential handling, server-side project ownership enforced on every agent message, and sandboxed per-project preview tokens on the edge worker.

Resumable generation built on a per-job state table records which files were committed before an interruption and restarts from that boundary on the next attempt, so a provider timeout or client disconnect does not discard work in progress.

A separate runtime worker handles full-stack user-generated applications by compiling agent-produced code into named hosted worker scripts, managing hot-reload file pushes, enforcing per-project lifetime and crash recovery, and returning a live accessible address to the workspace preview.

Gallery search was upgraded from keyword filtering to semantic nearest-neighbour queries by embedding each project's name and description, storing the vectors in a dedicated index, and returning scored results ranked by similarity on every search request.

Operators can register an external model provider with a compatible address and encrypted key; the registry validates the address against the outbound-request guard, stores the configuration, and routes generation traffic to the custom provider alongside the built-in model set.
defect_repairs: An aborted streaming generation would silently restart on an alternative provider path and still commit partial files to the database; fixed by broadcasting the interruption event before bumping the write epoch and placing epoch-ticket guards at every downstream file-write callsite.

The gallery remix handler compared a caller's live project count against the wrong limit threshold, allowing users who had reached their visible quota to keep creating remixes far beyond it; the fix was shipped with a regression test.

Repair state for the post-generation completeness loop was held only in memory and lost on serverless hibernation, causing the repair to restart from scratch on every wake; fixed by persisting it to a dedicated database table with lazy reload.

A preview iframe reload triggered an authentication error because the sandboxed iframe lacked access to the session token needed to re-authenticate; fixed by delegating the reload signal to the parent frame, which holds the token.
work_units: Replace the keyword-only gallery ordering with a ranking function that combines semantic similarity, recency, and remix count to return relevance-ordered results rather than purely newest-first, building on the existing vector index and scoring infrastructure.

Wrap the multi-file replace-all write sequence in a single database transaction so a partial failure leaves the project in its prior consistent state rather than half-applied, and extend the migration test suite to cover the rollback path.

Extend the post-generation route-coverage checker to recognise the conditional pathname dispatch style used by the baseline server template, removing false-positive repair passes for projects that follow that pattern instead of the chained-router style the checker currently understands.

Add a paginated per-user generation audit endpoint to the registry that records model, token counts, and timing for each generation event and lets operators query consumption history over any date range without querying the main analytics pipeline.
net_new_capabilities: Real-time collaborative editing would let multiple authenticated users in the same project receive the agent's file stream simultaneously and reconcile concurrent local edits against the shared write epoch, building on the websocket multiplexing and concurrency infrastructure already present.

A billing and subscription tier layer on the existing daily quota ledger would associate paid plans with higher generation limits, gate premium features behind plan checks, and update a user's tier on upgrade or cancellation via payment webhook.

A visual click-to-edit panel would let users change element styles, text, and properties directly in the live preview without writing a prompt, building on the inspect-mode element-selection infrastructure already wired into the workspace.

Version history with named checkpoints and rollback would let users return the project file tree to any prior snapshot, building on the source-snapshot hashing and storage infrastructure already used for publication and migration verification.

A plugin registry with sandboxed execution would let third-party developers publish agent tools available during generation, with per-tool permission scopes that users must approve before a tool is invoked on their project.
repo_evolutions: A multi-week security hardening campaign transformed the system from a zero-auth prototype into a hardened multi-tenant service by adding cryptographic sessions, server-side project ownership, sandboxed preview origins with isolation headers, a model allowlist, and an outbound-request guard.

The generation logic was extracted from a monolithic durable object into a standalone pipeline class, with the design constraint that any state surviving hibernation must be backed by database storage rather than in-memory fields.

The browser-based preview engine was replaced by an edge-native approach where user code runs inside a sandboxed iframe served from a separate worker origin with per-project tokens, isolation headers, and opaque-origin confinement, instead of a node runtime inside the browser.
performance_work: A combined lease-start and token-reservation operation was merged into a single atomic database write to the registry, removing one network round-trip per generation launch.

The system prompt and current file listing were placed at a stable prefix in the model context, enabling the provider's prompt-caching layer to avoid re-encoding the same preamble on every conversational turn in a long project.

A short-lived in-memory cache for the gallery listing in the registry eliminates repeated full-table scans on every public gallery page load, with a thirty-second time-to-live balancing freshness against read pressure.
A key-value session cache stores validated session records for authenticated requests, allowing the edge worker to skip a synchronous round-trip to the account registry on the hot authenticated path.
hardening_work: A multi-phase hardening pass introduced cryptographic session tokens, a server-enforced model allowlist with timeout guards, an outbound-request guard blocking private network targets, explicit allowed origins on all preview messages, and a content-security policy on the application shell.

A shared write guard enforced across all file-write paths checks the current write epoch before committing any file, so no generation can clobber files written by a newer generation that started after the user clicked stop.

Bot protection was added to the authentication endpoints by requiring a server-side verification token that proves each request was submitted by a human in a real browser rather than an automated script.
A per-minute rate limit on live-file push messages from the runtime worker to connected clients prevents a runaway build process from saturating the communication channel.
integration_work: A hosted-worker runtime integration manages the full publication lifecycle for user-generated applications, including creating and deleting named hosted scripts, assigning public slugs, managing custom domain records, and returning the live address to the workspace.

Export to a version-control host was built as a multi-step flow that zips the current file tree, obtains a short-lived token via a third-party login handshake, then creates or updates a remote repository.

A generation metrics integration writes structured data points for every completed generation, including model, token counts, latency stages, and outcome, to a dedicated analytics dataset, enabling operator-level reporting without querying the main project database.

Transactional email delivery was routed through a queue-based system with automatic retries on transient failures, and an admin endpoint exposes the current delivery health so operators can detect silent email drops.

material.material_summary: This codebase is a multi-tenant artificial intelligence application builder deployed on an edge serverless platform, where users describe an application and the system generates, hosts, and continuously repairs a full-stack web application on their behalf. The most substantial engineering is in the generation pipeline and its correctness invariants: resumable multi-step tool loops, write-epoch concurrency guards, transactional quota accounting, and a post-generation validation layer for missing files and unimplemented routes. A parallel security hardening track transformed the system from a zero-auth prototype into a hardened multi-tenant service with cryptographic sessions, sandboxed preview origins, and an outbound-request guard.
material.what_i_could_not_assess: The hosted-worker runtime deployment could not be fully assessed without a live environment to verify named-script lifecycle and custom-domain binding under production conditions.
